Jargonic Sets New Standards for Japanese ASR
May 6, 2025
Gil Hetz
Jargonic Sets New Standards for Japanese ASR
日本語で話そう。Jargonic is ready.
Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems often excel in lab conditions but struggle in real-world enterprise environments—especially when it comes to linguistically complex languages like Japanese. Unlike English, Japanese doesn’t use whitespace (the spaces between words in a sentence) to separate words, making Word Error Rate (WER) less relevant as a benchmark. Instead, Character Error Rate (CER) becomes the primary metric for evaluating transcription quality.
On top of that, Japanese blends three diverse writing systems-–hiragana, katakana, and kanji–, with hundreds of honorific structures, and shifting pronunciations based on context. For example, the word “three” sounds different when referring to people, flat objects, or animals. Combined with dense domain-specific jargon, these intricacies make Japanese one of the most challenging languages for ASR to master. With the release of Jargonic V2, aiOla continues to break through these barriers.
After setting new benchmarks in English, Spanish, French, and more, Jargonic V2 now leads in Japanese as well—delivering not just superior transcription accuracy, but also unmatched recall of specialized terms across industries like manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and finance.
Going Beyond Transcription: Why Jargon Recall Matters
Most ASR models today are “universal scribes”—trained for broad transcription accuracy but unfit for recognizing the acronyms, product names, and technical terminology found in real-world enterprise settings. That’s where Jargonic stands apart.
Our proprietary Keyword Spotting (KWS) technology allows Jargonic to identify domain-specific terms without the need for retraining or manually curated vocab lists. Unlike traditional models, which may stumble when encountering niche or industry-specific words, Jargonic detects them in real-time—thanks to a context-aware, zero-shot learning mechanism deeply integrated into the ASR pipeline.
Benchmark Results: Jargonic vs. the Field
We tested Jargonic V2 on two Japanese datasets (both includes all three primary Japanese scripts kanji, hiragana, and katakana):
CommonVoice v.13
– a standard dataset that tests general speech recognition capabilities.
ReazonSpeech
– Diverse set of natural Japanese speech, collected from terrestrial television streams.
Across both datasets, Jargonic outperformed Whisper v3, ElevenLabs, Deepgram, and AssemblyAI in key areas:
Jargonic delivered a 94.7% recall rate for domain-specific Japanese terms—meaning it correctly detected nearly all specialized jargon without training. No other model came close.
Even in natural, unstructured Japanese speech (Reazon dataset), Jargonic outperformed every other model—cutting character error rate (CER) in half or better.
Built for the Real World
These results aren’t just academic. They highlight a fundamental capability for enterprises operating in multilingual, jargon-heavy environments: the ability to capture accurate, structured data from spoken interactions—no matter the language, context, or complexity.
With Jargonic, speech becomes a reliable interface for enterprise AI—not just for transcription, but for real-time understanding and action.
Author
Gil Hetz
Gil Hetz is the Vice President of Research at aiOla, where he spearheads the company’s technology, intellectual property, and innovation initiatives. With over 15 years of expertise in Engineering and Machine Learning, Gill holds a Ph.D. from Texas A&M University. Gil has a robust professional background that includes significant roles in both academia and industry. Before joining aiOla, he served as a SaaS Product Manager at QRI, where he led the Forecasting Technology Team. In this role, he was instrumental in developing a fit-for-purpose modeling toolbox, which integrated both data-driven and simulation-based forecasting capabilities.
Earlier in his career, Gill completed a Postdoctoral fellowship in Model Calibration and Efficient Reservoir Imaging (MCERI), during which he developed various advanced forecasting techniques. His extensive experience and innovative contributions have positioned him as a leader in the fields of engineering and machine learning.

data.title: Migrating a JavaScript Project from Prettier and ESLint to BiomeJS
data.author: unripe_syntax
data.article_summary: BiomeJS是一款新兴的JavaScript工具，旨在替代Prettier和ESLint，通过集成代码格式化和代码检查功能，简化工作流并提升性能。它源自于已终止的Rome项目，但已发展成独立的工具链，使用Rust编写，具备多线程能力，速度比Prettier快25倍，比ESLint快15倍。Biome的格式化功能与Prettier类似，但语言支持较少；其代码检查功能受ESLint启发，支持自定义规则和多语言。安装和使用简单，通过NPM分发，无需配置文件即可开始使用。Biome通过`format`和`lint`命令分别进行代码格式化和检查，并提供详细的错误和警告信息。是否从Prettier和ESLint迁移到Biome，取决于项目需求和语言支持情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rome/BiomeJS 及其与 Prettier、ESLint 等工具的比较

不同观点：
• **jemmyw** 认为 Rome 项目在实际推出可用工具前就引起了大量关注和讨论，这让他感到困惑。他认为 Rome 是一个没有实际工具支撑的“理念”，并将其与 Prettier 的渐进式发展做对比。jemmyw 还提到，开源项目可能需要先推出实际代码，才能获得更多关注和成长。

• **mrbluecoat** 持调侃态度，认为虽然 Rome/BiomeJS 试图通过集成工具来节省时间，但实际操作中节省的时间微乎其微，不值得大肆宣传。

• **egorfine** 对前端工具的快速变化表示失望，提到生态系统中的主要工具经常发生重大变化，例如 ESLint 的 flat config 以及 Airbnb 风格指南的弃用。他引用了“红皇后的赛跑”来形容前端开发中不断追赶新工具的局面，认为 BiomeJS（Rome 的延续）的死亡象征着前端开发工具的不稳定。

• **zoogeny** 提到在 TypeScript 项目中选择了 ESLint 和 Prettier 而不是 BiomeJS，因为前者更成熟和稳定。同时抱怨了 ESM 模块在 TypeScript 项目中的支持不佳，并表示如果 BiomeJS 改善 TypeScript 的支持，未来可能会考虑使用。

• **progx** 认为 Prettier 和 ESLint 已经足够好用，虽然 BiomeJS 尝试将两者功能合并，但在需要做一些自定义修改时，Prettier 仍然是更好的选择。

• **DGCA** 分享了团队使用 BiomeJS 遇到的问题，尤其是 CI 中出现的问题，导致团队最终换回 Prettier 和 ESLint，并且发现了很多之前未报告的问题。

• **sibeliuse** 分享了团队成功迁移到 BiomeJS 后遇到的一个问题：BiomeJS 无法正确格式化嵌入语言（如 GraphQL），最终他们保留了 Prettier 用于格式化，但继续使用 BiomeJS 进行 linting。

• **horsawlarway** 批评文章更像是营销材料，而不是实际的迁移指南，认为文章没有深入探讨迁移中的实际问题和成本，而只是强调了 BiomeJS 的速度优势，而这并不是开发者最关心的问题。

• **herpdyderp** 对 Prettier 的频繁 bug 和插件系统设计表示不满，希望有一个更可靠的替代工具。

• **rafram** 指出 BiomeJS 的性能优势可能与其功能集较少有关，暗示其尚未达到 ESLint 那样的成熟度。

• **Alifatisk** 是 BiomeJS 的支持者，认为它尝试将工具链统一为一个默认选项，询问其他人是否有使用经验和收益。

• **jmisavage** 表示好奇是否有开发者在大型项目中进行了这种迁移，并看到了实际的收益。

• **7bit** 提到 Prettier 在 HTML 格式化上的问题，认为其违反了 HTML 规范，对此感到不满。

• **nsonha** 质疑为什么 web 开发者会对选择 linter 等不太重要的事情大书特书，而在 AI 革命的背景下，其他编程语言社区似乎没有类似的讨论。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：BiomeJS 的实际效用和其在开发者中的受欢迎程度。部分开发者认为它解决了实际问题，而另一些开发者则认为其带来的性能提升和整合功能并不足以替代现有的成熟工具。
- **工具稳定性与成熟度**：许多开发者对 Prettier 和 ESLint 的成熟度、稳定性和广泛支持表示认可，但对 BiomeJS 的功能和稳定性仍有疑虑。
- **前端开发工具的快速变化**：一些开发者对前端工具的频繁变化和不稳定性表示失望，认为这增加了不必要的复杂性和工作量。

43913950.article_content:
Prettier and ESLint have long been indispensable tools in the JavaScript
ecosystem for ensuring code consistency and quality. They have become
staples in the toolchains of JavaScript projects worldwide.
However, a new player has emerged to challenge their dominance:
BiomeJS. This ambitious project seeks to combine the
functionality of both tools into a single, high-performance solution for code
formatting and linting.
By combining these capabilities, Biome aims to simplify workflows, reduce
configuration complexity, and significantly boost performance, thus positioning
itself as the next generation of JavaScript tooling.
In this article, I'll introduce the BiomeJS project, explore its setup, and help
you decide if migrating from Prettier and ESLint is the right move for you.
What Is Biome?
BiomeJS
started its life as a fork of the now-defunct
Rome project
, but has since evolved into its
own distinct toolchain focused on providing a fast, integrated development
experience.
It currently provides two solutions for JavaScript developers:
A Prettier-like code formatter.
A powerful linter that's inspired by ESLint.
By combining these tools into a single solution, Biome minimizes the need for
multiple configurations, thus creating a more seamless experience for
developers.
It is also built with a modern architecture, using Rust for speed and
multi-threading, making it more than an order of magnitude faster than its
predecessors.
In this way, it represents not only a replacement but also a significant leap
forward in simplifying and optimizing the JavaScript development workflow.
Comparison with Prettier
Biome's formatter, like Prettier's, offers only a few configuration options. Its
output is mostly compatible with Prettier — though there are some
differences
— and
it formats about
25 times faster
because it's multithreaded and written in Rust.
While
Biome supports multiple languages
,
it lags behind Prettier in terms of coverage. Notably, HTML, Markdown, and SCSS
are not yet supported, and frameworks like Vue, Astro, and Svelte have only
partial support.
Comparison with ESLint for JavaScript
Many of Biome's linting rules are inspired by ESLint and other popular linters,
and organized into specific categories. Like ESLint, these rules are fully
configurable, allowing you to disable any rule or enable only a subset.
You can customize how rule violations are handled, choosing whether they trigger
warnings or errors, and whether automatic fixes should be suggested. For
example:
JSON
{
"linter"
: {
"rules"
: {
"correctness"
: {
"noUnusedVariables"
: {
"level"
:
"error"
,
"fix"
:
"none"
}
},
"style"
: {
"useConst"
: {
"level"
:
"warn"
,
"fix"
:
"unsafe"
}
}
}
}
}
Biome's linter also extends beyond JavaScript/TypeScript by supporting other
languages. It includes several CSS linting rules from
stylelint-config-recommended
with more in development. For a full list of supported rules, refer to the
Biome documentation
.
In terms of performance,
Biome is over 15 times faster than ESLint
,
again thanks to its Rust-based, multi-threaded architecture.
Getting Started with Biome
Although Biome isn't written in JavaScript, its executable is distributed
through the
NPM registry
, so you
can easily install it through your preferred package manager:
Shell
npm
install
--save-dev
--save-exact
@biomejs/biome
After installation, you can access the
biome
executable by running:
Shell
npx
biome
--version
# Version: 1.9.2
Biome doesn't require a configuration file to get started, allowing you to use
it immediately after installation.
For demonstration purposes, here's a sample JavaScript file you can experiment
with:
JavaScript
// index.js
function
sayHello
(
name
){
if
(name){console.
log
(
"Hello, "
+
name
+
"!"
);}
else
{console.
log
(
"Hello, World!"
);}}
let
person
=
"John"
;
sayHello
(person);
Formatting with Biome
To format code, you can use the
format
command like this:
Shell
npx
biome
format
index.js
By default, the
format
command operates in a dry-run mode, displaying the
proposed changes in the terminal with unformatted code in red and the corrected
version in green.
If you're happy with the changes, apply them using the
--write
flag:
Shell
npx
biome
format
--write
index.js
You will see a confirmation message like this:
Shell
Formatted
1
file
in
840µs.
Fixed
1
file
Linting with Biome
Biome can also lint your project files with the
lint
command:
Shell
npx
biome
lint
index.js
If there are linting problems in the file, you will see the following output:
Linting issues are categorized into three levels:
info
,
warn
, and
error
.
The
lint
command exits with a non-zero code for error-level issues, but you
can treat warnings similarly by using the
--error-on-warnings
flag:
Shell
npx
biome
lint
--error-on-warnings
The linting output provides detailed explanations for why a rule was triggered
and how to resolve the issue.
Each issue is annotated with the file name, line number, the rule that was
violated, and a human-readable description

• **nsonha** 质疑为什么 web 开发者会对选择 linter 等不太重要的事情大书特书，而在 AI 革命的背景下，其他编程语言社区似乎没有类似的讨论。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：BiomeJS 的实际效用和其在开发者中的受欢迎程度。部分开发者认为它解决了实际问题，而另一些开发者则认为其带来的性能提升和整合功能并不足以替代现有的成熟工具。

- **前端开发工具的快速变化**：一些开发者对前端工具的频繁变化和不稳定性表示失望，认为这增加了不必要的复杂性和工作量。

data.title: Sandy Bridge-era motherboard gets M.2 SSD boot support 12 years after launch
data.author: mobilio
data.article_summary: Gigabyte发布了针对B75M-D3H主板的固件更新（F16f），主要用于修复2024年发现的PKfail漏洞。尽管该主板早在2012年推出，且已超出其生命周期，但新固件意外地增加了对从NVMe SSD（如M.2 SSD）启动的支持。这一功能原本是不支持的，因为主板仅有SATA接口。通过使用M.2到PCIe适配器，用户可以在老旧的B75M-D3H上利用NVMe驱动器，尽管在PCIe 2.0接口下性能有所降低。目前尚不清楚这一支持是无意中加入还是有意为之，但此举可能为其他老主板带来了类似功能。

43914677.article_content:
(Image credit: Gigabyte)
Firmware updates for motherboards aim to fix bugs and occasionally introduce new features. However,
Chinese netizen
WhiteCamellia (via
Uniko's Hardware
) found that manufacturers often fail to promote these new features. Notably, Gigabyte has seemingly updated the 13-year-old B75M-D3H motherboard to support booting from NVMe SSDs, like M.2 SSDs, a previously unavailable functionality.
Introduced in 2012, the B75M-D3H is a motherboard featuring the B75 chipset, designed to support Intel's 2nd Generation (
Sandy Bridge
) and 3rd Generation (
Ivy Bridge
) Core processors. Clearly, the motherboard is beyond its end-of-life (EOL) status.
Ancient but not forgotten, Gigabyte issued a new firmware (F16f) for the B75M-D3H motherboard in 2024 to address the
PKfail vulnerability
discovered in the same year. The update is particularly noteworthy, as the last firmware update (F15) received by the B75M-D3H was in 2013, over ten years prior. The F16f firmware primarily addresses the PKfail issue. However, WhiteCamellia identified an additional functionality. An analysis of the F16f firmware using UEFITool reveals the inclusion of the NVMe DXE trifecta (Nvme, NvmeSmm, NVMEINT13), which is essential for booting from NVMe drives, like M.2.
The B75M-D3H was not designed to accommodate NVMe SSDs. The motherboard features one SATA III and five SATA II connectors for storage, explaining its initial lack of support for booting from NVMe drives. Nonetheless, users can employ M.2 to PCIe adapters, allowing M.2 drives to connect with the motherboard via its expansion ports. That is precisely the approach WhiteCamellia took to use his
Western Digital WD SN740
with the B75M-D3H motherboard.
The SN740 is a PCIe 4.0 x4 SSD that provides sequential read and write speeds of up to 2,000 MB/s. When installed on a slower interface, it logically results in reduced performance. On the B75M-D3H motherboard, the SN740 operates at PCIe 2.0 x4 speeds. This limitation is not due to the motherboard itself, as the B75M-D3H has a fully functional PCIe 3.0 x16 expansion slot. However, when paired with a
Sandy Bridge
processor, that slot operates at PCIe 2.0 speeds, which we suspect is the case with WhiteCamellia.
PCIe 2.0 storage speeds may seem underwhelming in modern times, considering PCIe 5.0 drives have
been around for a couple of years now
. However, the transition from SATA III to PCIe 2.0 is quite substantial and could revive aging systems to bring some snappiness to the operating system and everyday applications.
For quite some time, enthusiasts have modified firmware to enable unsupported processors or SSDs to function with newer motherboards. Regarding the B75M-D3H, it's unclear whether Gigabyte intentionally or unintentionally provided NVMe boot support. The PKfail vulnerability impacts numerous Intel platforms, covering the 60-series to 100-series chipsets, all of which received firmware updates from Gigabyte in September 2024. It's possible that this new firmware introduced similar functionality to other older motherboards aside from the B75M-D3H.

data.title: Optimizing Common Lisp
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用SBCL内置的统计性能分析工具**sb-sprof**来优化Common Lisp代码，重点分析CPU和内存分配的瓶颈。作者通过分析**parcom/json**模块，成功将运行速度提升了3倍，并将内存分配减少了25倍。文章详细说明了如何使用`with-profiling`宏在CPU模式和内存模式下进行性能分析，识别出如`consume`等热点函数。通过优化技术，如避免不必要的工作、使用`simple-string`和`schar`、多返回值、栈分配和Lambda缓存，有效提升了性能。最终，作者强调了数据驱动优化决策的重要性，而不是仅凭猜测进行优化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Common Lisp（CL）代码优化的不同观点和工具使用建议

不同观点：
• [metroholografix] 认为新手在CL代码中经常使用 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 0))` 是一种不好的习惯，虽然可以提高速度，但会牺牲安全性，例如去掉数组边界检查和类型检查。他建议使用 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 1))`，认为这样在大多数情况下能保持相近的性能，同时保留必要的安全检查。此外，他还推荐了SBCL中的sb-simd库，以及通过编译器宏和VM内部钩子进行自定义代码生成的方法。

• [dom2] 补充了关于性能分析工具的具体使用建议，指出在使用 `sb-sprof` 进行性能分析后，可以调用 `(disassemble '<profiled function>)` 来查看增强的汇编代码，并显示每个指令的采样命中比例，这有助于进一步优化代码。

• [mark_l_watson] 对上述内容表示感谢，并提到自己曾在LispWorks Pro中进行过性能分析，但尚未在SBCL中尝试。他还顺便提到了对metroholografix提到的烹饪页面的赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[metroholografix] 明确反对新手过度优化代码时牺牲安全性，认为 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 0))` 是一种坏习惯。虽然没有直接的反对意见，但[mark_l_watson] 和 [dom2] 的回复更侧重于工具使用和实践经验，没有直接回应此观点。

• 工具和实践：讨论中提到了多个具体的工具和库，如 `sb-simd`、`sb-sprof` 和 `(disassemble ...)`，这些工具可以帮助开发者更好地进行性能分析和优化。

• 实际操作建议：[metroholografix] 提供了具体的优化建议和替代方案，[dom2] 则补充了性能分析后如何查看汇编代码的具体操作步骤，提供了实用性的指导。

43913727.article_content:
Table of Contents
Introduction to sb-sprof
time
with-profiling: CPU Mode
with-profiling: Memory Mode
Optimization Techniques
Avoiding Work
simple-string and schar
Multiple Return Values
Stack Allocation
Lambda Caching
Conclusion
Optimizing Common Lisp
By Colin on 2025-05-07
I recently released a
Parser Combinator library
for Common Lisp, but was unhappy with its performance. This article is a description of how I used
sb-sprof
, built in to SBCL, to identify both CPU and memory allocation hotspots, improving the runtime speed of the
parcom/json
module by 3x and decreasing memory allocation by 25x.
Introduction to sb-sprof
SBCL has a number of built-in extension libraries.
sb-sprof
is a "statistical profiler" that periodically samples the call stack to see where time is being spent and who is doing the most allocating. In my
parcom/benchmarks
system, I have:
(require :sb-sprof)
;; OVERALL
(let ((s (uiop:read-file-string "tests/data/large-file.json")))
(time (pj:parse s)))
;; SPEED
(let ((s (uiop:read-file-string "tests/data/large-file.json")))
(sb-sprof:with-profiling (:max-samples 100000 :sample-interval 0.00001 :report :graph)
(aref (pj:parse s) 0)))
;; MEMORY
(let ((s (uiop:read-file-string "tests/data/large-file.json")))
(sb-sprof:with-profiling (:max-samples 100000 :sample-interval 0.00001 :report :graph :mode :alloc)
(aref (pj:parse s) 0)))
Like
time
, just by wrapping a call with
with-profiling
we can interactively profile any function we wish.
time
time
itself is available in any CL implementation and is a quick way to gauge the overall performance of something. Running the
OVERALL
form above, we see:
Evaluation took:
0.881 seconds of real time
0.877017 seconds of total run time (0.867189 user, 0.009828 system)
[ Real times consist of 0.079 seconds GC time, and 0.802 seconds non-GC time. ]
[ Run times consist of 0.078 seconds GC time, and 0.800 seconds non-GC time. ]
99.55% CPU
2,474,196,347 processor cycles
261,309,152 bytes consed
Before I started optimizing,
time
was reporting 6.5 billion bytes consed, which is where the "25x reduction" stat comes from.
with-profiling: CPU Mode
Evaluting the
SPEED
form above, we see:
Self        Total        Cumul
Nr  Count     %  Count     %  Count     %    Calls  Function
------------------------------------------------------------------------
1    159  19.4    270  33.0    159  19.4        -  (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CONSUME)
2     73   8.9     73   8.9    232  28.3        -  SB-KERNEL:TWO-ARG->=
3     63   7.7     67   8.2    295  36.0        -  PJ::ESCAPED
4     55   6.7     55   6.7    350  42.7        -  (LAMBDA (PJ::C) :IN PJ:STRING)
5     39   4.8     45   5.5    389  47.5        -  (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CHAR)
6     38   4.6     76   9.3    427  52.1        -  PC:CHAR
7     37   4.5     37   4.5    464  56.7        -  SB-IMPL::GETHASH/EQL-HASH
8     33   4.0     48   5.9    497  60.7        -  PC:CONSUME
9     27   3.3     27   3.3    524  64.0        -  SB-IMPL::GETHASH/EQ-HASH/FLAT
10     18   2.2    405  49.5    542  66.2        -  PJ:STRING
...
And so on. Perhaps the most relevant column here is
Self %
, which tells us how much of the total runtime was spent inside the named function. In this case we see it spending the most time within the innards of the
consume
parser. "Data ends arguments" as they say, so it is helpful to know where the time is actually being spent as opposed to guessing. Here, it wouldn't make sense for me to optimize
string
(only 2% of the total) when
consume
is so clearly a hotspot.
Normally the
:report
mode is
:flat
, but by setting it to
:graph
we are shown where each function is called from, and what it calls:
Callers
Total.     Function
Count     %  Count     %      Callees
------------------------------------------------------------------------
3   0.4                   (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CONSUME) [1]
35   4.3                   PJ::SKIP-SPACE [17]
1   0.1                   (LAMBDA (#:*>-OFFSET2) :IN PC:BETWEEN) [11]
159  19.4    270  33.0   (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CONSUME) [1]
1   0.1                   PC:CONSUME [8]
3   0.4                   (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CONSUME) [1]
4   0.5                   PC::OFF [23]
6   0.7                   PC:SPACE? [22]
50   6.1                   (LAMBDA (PJ::C) :IN PJ:STRING) [4]
47   5.7                   SB-KERNEL:TWO-ARG->= [2]
------------------------------------------------------------------------
...
And so on. Here it looks like it's often being used to skip over whitespace.
with-profiling: Memory Mode
By adding
:mode :alloc
, the output of
with-profiling
becomes memory-focused.
Self        Total        Cumul
Nr  Count     %  Count     %  Count     %    Calls  Function
------------------------------------------------------------------------
1   6282  74.3   6282  74.3   6282  74.3        -  ALLOC-TRAMP
2   1177  13.9   1177  13.9   7459  88.3        -  SYS-ALLOC-TRAMP
3    989  11.7    989  11.7   8448 100.0        -  LIST-ALLOC-TRAMP
4      2   0.0

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：合同软件开发中的客户获取方式及相关挑战

不同观点：
• **[rmah]** 认为客户获取主要依赖声誉、推荐和个人网络，客户最大的风险是项目交付失败或结果不理想。开发人员不仅需要技术能力，还要建立信任和可靠性，并应主动抵制模糊或不断变化的需求，以确保项目成功。

• **[arevno]** 支持声誉和个人网络对于客户获取的重要性，提到他们的合同大多是通过自我推荐或声誉推荐获得的。他还分享了一个策略，即从全职雇主辞职后立即被雇主保留为客户，以此作为启动业务的方式。

• **[alexdowad]** 指出，如果公司存在足够长时间，通常会有长期客户反复寻求软件修改、新增功能和维护，这些客户也会介绍新客户。

• **[Smeevy]** 强调最有效的方式是利用现有的人脉并在客户讨论需要解决方案时"在房间里"参与讨论。

• **[ramesh31]** 对声誉和联系人列表的建议提出质疑，认为这些建议没有回答如何从零开始获取客户的问题。

• **[andrewmcwatters]** 分享了自己的经验，通过与有本地历史的开发人员合作，以及多年在行业内的工作经历，通过口碑获得业务。他还提到通过发布设计和开发笔记、获得媒体出版和行业奖项来吸引客户。此外，他们通过研发投入开发竞争性技术，以保持业务的独特性和竞争力。

补充讨论：
• **[neil5paul]** 提到通过在线社区、LinkedIn和电子邮件营销作为获取客户的手段。

争议焦点：
• 如何从无到有建立客户群是讨论中的一个争议点，尤其是对新进入者而言。
• 声誉和个人网络的作用被广泛认可，但有人质疑这些是否足够或如何实现。

总的来说，讨论围绕着合同软件开发中客户获取的不同策略，包括声誉和个人网络的重要性、销售团队的作用、以及从零开始建立客户群的挑战。

data.title: Cybercrime operation traced back to Myanmar warlord
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: 美国财政部指控缅甸克伦地区军阀Saw Chit Thu及其子Saw Htoo Eh Moo和Saw Chit Chi运营一个大型网络犯罪集团，涉及诈骗、网络犯罪、洗钱和人口贩卖。该团伙通过非正式的呼叫中心实施多种诈骗，包括“杀猪盘”恋爱诈骗、加密货币投资骗局等，并为朝鲜政府提供洗钱服务。尽管美国对其实施制裁，但由于该集团主要使用地下加密货币交易，且受缅甸军政府保护，制裁的短期影响有限。受害者多为西方个人和企业，损失高达数十亿美元。

43914652.article_content:
Identity
,
Governance, Risk and Compliance
,
Government Regulations
Massive cybercrime operation traced back to Myanmar warlord
May 6, 2025
Share
By
Shaun
Nichols
(Adobe Stock)
An international cybercrime operation was traced back to an unlikely source: a warlord controlling a remote part of Myanmar.
The
U.S. Department of Treasury
said it believed Saw Chit Thu and his sons Saw Htoo Eh Moo and Saw Chit Chi were using their control over the Karen region of Myanmar bordering Thailand to operate a hub for fraud and cybercrime activities.
All three are now subject to U.S. government sanctions aimed at limiting their ability to access accounts and perform financial transactions.
Running a series of unofficial call center facilities, it is alleged that the group has been carrying out a number of scam operations, ranging from
“pig butchering” romance scams
against individuals to business-focused schemes such as
cryptocurrency investment scams
and money laundering fronts for sanctioned groups.
The patriarch of the Saw family, Saw Chit Thu commands a militia known as the Karen National Army along with Saw Htoo Eh Moo and Saw Chit Chit. The group’s region of control is said to run along a key border region between Myanmar and Thailand, allowing the group to control access between the two countries.
True to their namesake, the Karen National Army are a decidedly unpleasant group. In addition to running a cyberfraud hub, it is believed that the militia is engaging in human trafficking, smuggling, and various other dirty deeds performed at the behest of Myanmar’s military junta.
While the jungles of Myanmar may seem like an unlikely place to find a crybercrime empire, the location and political climate of the area makes for fertile ground in terms of operating criminal enterprises. It is believed that in the U.S. alone between $2 billion and $3.5 billion was lost to cybercrime operations originating in Myanmar over the last three years.
Because of its regional control and close ties to the military government, officials say that the KNA established itself in the human trafficking and cybercrime landscape, with the two areas often overlapping as foreign nationals are lured in with offers of call center work only to find themselves unwilling employees in a fraud factory.
The U.S. government said the captive workers are subject to additional abuse and mistreatment as they help carry out various fraud operations at the militia’s behest, usually targeting individuals and organizations in the West.
The schemes can range from
romance scams
in which fake profiles are used to trick would-be daters into handing over their money and personally identifiable information, to investment fraud schemes that target businesses and investors with the promise of a lucrative payback in the form of cryptocurrency profits which are, of course, never realized.
In some cases, the scams are so elaborate as to include multiple rounds of investments and the use of fake transactions to trick the targets into believing that their investments are already seeing returns over a series of months before the rug is finally pulled.
It is also alleged that the group has been offering its money laundering services to
the North Korean government
, allowing the dictatorship to convert
stolen cryptocurrency
into seemingly legit assets and transactions.
While the sanctions will freeze any and all U.S.-based assets held by the KNA and prohibit transactions as a criminal enterprise, it will likely have little short-term impact for a group that operates largely in underground cryptocurrency transactions and enjoys the protection of a military dictatorship.

data.title: Removal of Deepin Desktop from OpenSUSE Due to Packaging Policy Violation
data.author: milliams
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了openSUSE中Deepin桌面环境（DDE）的包装策略违规问题。Deepin社区包装者通过一个“许可证协议”对话框绕过了SUSE安全团队的审查要求，擅自安装受限制的D-Bus服务和Polkit策略文件。这种行为违反了openSUSE的包装政策。

文章回顾了Deepin组件在openSUSE中的审查历史，指出自2017年以来，多个Deepin组件的审查问题未得到妥善解决。2021年引入的deepin-feature-enable包通过让用户接受“许可证”来绕过安全审查，安装未被批准的组件。

由于这些违规行为，openSUSE决定暂时移除Deepin桌面包。文章还讨论了未来如何解决此问题，包括用户如何继续在openSUSE上使用Deepin。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenSUSE在软件包分发和审核流程中的标准和一致性问题

不同观点：
• **[对OpenSUSE审核流程的担忧]**  
[remram] 表达了对OpenSUSE分发不符合其政策的软件包的担忧。他认为，Linux发行版应该比应用商店更具有一致性和严格的审核流程，当前这种情况让人对其可信度产生怀疑。

• **[对OpenSUSE提供Deepin安装指南的质疑]**  
[GuinansEyebrows] 则关注OpenSUSE对Deepin软件的处理方式，认为如果OpenSUSE对软件的分发有强烈立场，就不应提供特定平台的安装步骤，而应由Deepin自己负责文档和安装指导。

补充讨论：
• **[争议焦点：审核一致性与实际操作的矛盾]**  
评论之间的争议焦点在于OpenSUSE在软件审核和分发上的标准不一致。一方面是对未审核软件包被分发的担忧，另一方面是对OpenSUSE在提供安装指导上的操作与其审核立场的矛盾。

• **[具体例子：Deepin软件的分发与文档]**  
具体讨论了Deepin软件，一个可能不符合OpenSUSE政策的软件，却被提供了详细的安装指南，引发了对OpenSUSE审核流程透明度和一致性的进一步质疑。

这两个观点共同指向了OpenSUSE在软件审核和用户指导方面的潜在问题，尤其是在一致性和可信度方面。

4) Conclusions about the Future of Deepin in openSUSE

1) Introduction
The
Deepin desktop environment
(DDE) is part of the Deepin
Linux distribution. It focuses on usability, a polished graphical presentation
and support for the Chinese language. It is also available on a number of
other Linux distributions, openSUSE among them.
Recently we noticed a policy violation in the packaging of the Deepin desktop
environment in openSUSE. To get around security review requirements, our
Deepin community packager implemented a workaround which bypasses the regular
RPM packaging mechanisms to install restricted assets.
As a result of this violation, and in the light of the difficult history we
have with Deepin code reviews, we will be removing the Deepin Desktop packages
from openSUSE distributions for the time being.
In this blog post we will look at the exact nature of the policy violation,
the review history of Deepin components in openSUSE and the conclusions we
draw from all of this. Finally, we will give an outlook on how this situation
could be resolved, and how users of openSUSE can continue to opt-in to use
Deepin in the future.
2) Bypass of the openSUSE Packaging Policy via a âLicense Agreementâ Dialog
The SUSE security team enforces a number of
packaging
restrictions
for openSUSE distributions. Among
others, the installation of D-Bus system service configuration files and Polkit
policies requires a review by us. When we are satisfied with a packageâs
security, then we whitelist the respective components. From there on, the
package can be submitted to the
openSUSE:Factory
project in the
Open Build
Service
, which is the base for the openSUSE
Tumbleweed rolling release distribution.
For a large software suite like Deepin, which contains a significant number of
D-Bus services, this can be a difficult initial hurdle to overcome. We have
been in contact with the openSUSE Deepin packager ever since 2017, and have
whitelisted various Deepin D-Bus components in the meantime. A number of
remaining Deepin review bugs have seen little progress in recent years,
however, because the issues we pointed out have not been addressed properly.
Perhaps tired of waiting, the packager decided to try a different avenue to
get the remaining Deepin components into openSUSE skirting the review
requirements. In January 2025, during routine reviews, we stumbled upon
the
deepin-feature-enable
package,
which was introduced
on
2021-04-27
without consulting
us or even informing us. This innocently named package implements a âlicense
agreement dialogâ which basically explains that the SUSE security team has
doubts about the security of Deepin, but to properly use Deepin, certain
components need to be installed anyway. Thus, if the user does not care about
security then âthe licenseâ should be accepted. If the user accepts, the
missing D-Bus configuration files and Polkit policies are automatically
extracted into system directories from tarballs found in the
deepin-daemon-dbus
and
deepin-daemon-polkit
packages. The license text
also contains a hint suggesting to manually install the
deepin-file-manager-dbus
and
deepin-file-manager-polkit
packages and run a
script to sideload further configuration files that are needed for the Deepin
file manager D-Bus component to work.
The "license agreement" dialog presented by deepin-feature-enable.
For end users, this effectively means that typing âyâ once during the
installation of the Deepin pattern is enough to opt in to activating
components with questionable security which have not been accepted by the SUSE
security team.
Given the number of reviews that happened over many years, with some decline
in frequency and activity, we had wrongly assumed that by now the bulk of
Deepin D-Bus components had managed to enter
openSUSE:Factory
after being
whitelisted by us (apart from some optional utility packages). Instead we had
to find out that core components, which are found in the
deepin-daemon
package, had never been submitted for our review, but had been smuggled into
openSUSE.

data.title: "Police state" search got censored in Italy
data.author: richsnipe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何验证和传播关于“Italia è uno stato di polizia”的搜索结果以及可能的 censorship 问题

不同观点：
• [hiryuken] 认为通过各种搜索引擎（包括Google和Bing）搜索“Italia è uno stato di polizia”都能找到大量文章和信息，且使用VPN与否不影响搜索结果，因此认为不存在 censorship 问题。不过，他表示理解并部分共享对于 censorship 的担忧。
  
• [A_D_E_P_T] 提出可能很难将此问题引起广泛关注，建议通过创建意大利语博客或Substack，并向相关受众推广来增加曝光。他还建议联系Google的欧盟办公室并寻求法律意见以获得澄清。同时，A_D_E_P_T 提出另一种可能性，即当前的情况可能并非阴谋论，而是由于Google近年来质量下降（使用“enshittification”一词描述），并指出使用引号搜索可能会得到不同且更好的结果。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否存在对“Italia è uno stato di polizia”相关内容的 censorship。hiryuken 否认 censorship 的存在，而 A_D_E_P_T 则提出技术问题或内容劣化的可能性，并给出实际行动建议。
  
• A_D_E_P_T 强调了公民博客和个人行动的潜在影响力，表明通过个人努力可能可以更有效地传播和澄清此问题。

• 搜索技巧（如使用引号）被提及作为改善搜索结果的一种方法，这可能暗示搜索算法的局限性或差异。

43912713.article_content:
tl;dr - You can find the Youtube Timemachine browser extension on the
Chrome Web Store
and
Mozilla Add Ons
.
How this happened
Did you know that the average YouTube video is viewed about 41 times? For a platform that seemingly features professional content creators and is the second most visited site after Google, this view count might seem disappointing. Or is something else going on? I’ll explain how this fact inspired me to create a browser extension that makes visible the videos that the YouTube algorithm keeps hidden.
The videos no one sees
I read an article on BBC “
The hidden world beneath the shadows of YouTube’s algorithm
”, written on the occasion of YouTube’s 20th anniversary. It provides a fascinating alternative perspective on the video platform. Not about the big channels, successful influencers, or the platform’s role in online conversations, but more about the essence of YouTube as a personal video platform. With billions of videos that have never been viewed or only rarely seen. Author Thomas Germain references
a study
by Ethan Zuckerman, among others. Zuckerman is the director of the Institute for Digital Public Infrastructure and primarily a
blogger
. The research shows that the median number of views for videos is just 41 times. This means most videos in the dataset have been viewed less than or equal to 41 times. Moreover, if your video has more than 130 views, you’re in the top 30% of the most popular content on the platform.
The findings of the study reminded me of a website that Germain also references,
IMG_0001
by Riley Walz. Here you can find videos uploaded between 2009 and 2012 with iPhones that kept their standard file name, IMG_ followed by 4 numbers. These videos weren’t optimized for viewers but were meant to be quickly uploaded online to share with someone else. They are small snapshots of life, made public via the video service.
I realized there must be more videos from other cameras with a similar fixed structure in the filename and with few views on YouTube. I used to have a Sony Cybershot, which started file names with DSC_. There must be videos on YouTube in the format DSC_xxxx.
The idea
Then the idea came to me: Wouldn’t it be nice to have a browser extension to search through these videos?
I proposed the idea to the AI app
Openrouter
, which allows me to automatically communicate with different models depending on the question. I had never made a browser extension before, so I had the service explain it step by step.
After 30 minutes, I had a local Chrome extension that did exactly what I wanted.
You choose a date and a camera model. The code converts the month and day into four digits. So today would be 0501, and it combines this with the chosen model in a search query for YouTube. Then it immediately shows the results in YouTube. Here you can see videos with the title
DSC_0501
or here are videos made with a GoPro that have the filename
GOPR1127
. You can also select a random model and number with the Timewarp button.
I chose to use a date as a starting point to generate the four digits. The extension doesn’t search for videos that were posted with specific models on specific dates. Is that unclear? Let me know.
The results are as surprising as in Germain’s article. There are dashcams with 15 views, a young skier with 2 views, or a performance by three young friends
viewed only once
. The
calming waterfalls
of Allagash, Maine.
Some videos have never been viewed as you scroll through the list, some already have hundreds of views. But they are almost all videos free from call to actions, “like and subscribe” icons, and polished productions. They are glimpses into the daily lives of people around the world. They are videos that don’t have the pretension that the creator wants to be an influencer on social media. They are personal messages where the maker uses the tools at hand, like quickly making a video, uploading it, and sharing it privately.
YouTube
likes to call itself
the epicenter of popular culture and the new Hollywood. I prefer to see it as public infrastructure for people who want to tell a story, regardless of how many viewers they have.
How to make a browser extension
I had never made a browser extension before, so I first had Deepseek explain to me how they work. Then the model started creating the extension, constantly making adjustments based on my instructions.
Finally, AI helped me understand how to publish a browser extension on the
Chrome Web Store
and
Mozilla Add Ons
.
Everything is relatively simple. You can find, download, and modify the
complete code
on Github.
With AI’s help, I went from idea to launch in less than 90 minutes. Most of the time was spent creating the right icons and filling out forms at Mozilla and Google to publish the extension. AI did all the basic work. I did review the code myself. Because it’s relatively simple, I can assess whether it does what it’s supposed to do. data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对不同技术产品及其版本的评价与反馈

不同观点：
• [pjmlp] 认为 dBase III Plus 是其进入数据库编程世界的起点，随后使用了 Clipper Summer '87，并提到 C++ 的面向对象编程对 Clipper 5.x 的影响。他还指出，在习惯了早期的数据库操作方式后，适应 SQL 的记录导航和搜索方式有一定困难。

• [jansan] 对产品发布策略持批评态度，暗示 rushed 发布有缺陷的第四版可能会引发客户的负面反应，隐含对产品质量和发布流程的不满。

• [actionfromafar] 关注视频质量，猜测视频来源是 U-matic 磁带或 LaserDisc，并提到在视频的特定时间点有画质问题（如19分钟时的“雪花”现象），暗示可能是存储介质的质量问题。

补充讨论：
• [pjmlp] 提供了对数据库技术演变的个人历史视角，强调了从早期数据库系统到更现代的 SQL 系统的转变和适应难度。

• [jansan] 的评论中隐含了对软件产品版本发布的质量控制问题的担忧，特别是未完成版本的发布可能会损害用户信任。

• [actionfromafar] 则关注于视频技术及其保存质量，讨论了可能导致视频质量下降的技术原因（如介质老化）。

争议焦点：
• 产品发布的质量与客户反馈之间的矛盾，特别是在软件行业中发布未完善版本的风险。

data.title: Rage of the Oligarchs Naomi Klein: 'What They Want Is Absolutely Everything
data.author: mindracer
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了社会活动家、作家Naomi Klein的思想和作品。Klein以其对企业权力、气候变化、经济和政治的深刻分析而闻名，她的著作《休克主义》探讨右翼精英如何利用危机推动不受欢迎的经济议程，而《改变一切：资本主义与气候》则审视自由市场教条如何加速对地球的威胁。她最近关注阴谋文化以及科技亿万富翁如Elon Musk和Peter Thiel的黑暗世界观，认为这些人在引导特朗普政府时，放弃了对集体未来的积极愿景，转而为社会崩溃做准备。

Klein还讨论了特朗普的贸易战及其对科学的攻击，认为这是“休克主义”的一种表现，目的是利用危机推动有利于精英的政策。她指出，这种策略并非新现象，而是右翼长期利用危机推动议程的手段。总体而言，Klein强调当前政治和社会处于极端阶段，需要警惕和抵抗。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对政治、经济现状及其背后动因的看法

不同观点：
• [jayemar] 对阅读采访兴趣不大，更倾向于阅读具体的文章链接（《卫报》4月13日的文章）。其立场主要集中在对信息来源的偏好，并未深入讨论政治或经济问题，只是表达了信息获取方式的选择。

• [tastyface] 认为某些政治领袖（如Thiel）存在自相矛盾的行为：一方面支持全球政府，另一方面参与巩固保守精英的政治活动。tastyface 暗示这些领袖没有意识到自身的矛盾，甚至将这种行为与宗教中的反基督形象联系起来，认为这些领袖可能会引发“世界末日”式的局面，建议对这些领袖进行“制度化”。

• [meesles] 认为美国存在“偶像崇拜”文化，将富人置于高位，这种文化导致人们将“美国梦”等同于致富，从而使得权力和财富成为唯一追求。meesles 批评资本主义体系，认为其本质是“癌症”，因为它鼓励无休止的权力和财富扩张，进一步加剧了社会问题。

• [PicassoCTs] 认为有些人无法意识到世界的 dysfunction（功能失调）其实源自他们自己，而是习惯于将问题归咎于外部因素（如国家、持不同意见者）。当这些人掌握了全部控制权后，他们会用尽借口，转向阴谋论，认为到处都有叛徒阻碍他们的“理想社会”。PicassoCTs 暗示这种极端思维只会导致社会僵化，最终达成的结果与预期完全相反。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于对精英政治和资本主义体系的看法。tastyface 和 meesles 都批评了当前政治和经济体系中的问题，但 tastyface 聚焦于具体政治人物的矛盾行为，而 meesles 则更广泛地批评资本主义是社会问题的根源。
• PicassoCTs 的评论进一步扩展了讨论，指出某些人无法自我反省并将问题归咎于外部的倾向，揭示了政治理想和现实之间的冲突。
• 宗教元素在 tastyface 的评论中出现，将政治领袖的行为与宗教中的反基督形象联系起来，增添了讨论的戏剧性和极端性。

总体来看，评论者们对政治领袖的行为、资本主义体系以及社会 dysfunction 的根源存在明显分歧，尤其是对精英政治的看法和经济体系的批评成为讨论的核心。

Naomi Klein at Bedford Square Gardens on June 13, 2024 in London.

Wherever corporate power is running roughshod over culture, the
climate
, the economy, or our politics, progressives can count on Naomi Klein to provide a clear-eyed assessment of the damage and to offer pathways to resist with hope, rather than cower in despair.
A social activist and public intellectual, Klein is the author of
The Shock Doctrine
—
about how right-wing elites leverage moments of crisis to advance unpopular economic agendas — and
This Changes Everything: Capitalism Versus the Climate
, an examination of how free-market dogma is accelerating the threat to our planet’s survival. Her most recent book
Doppelganger
limns how conspiracy culture is shattering our notions of shared reality.
Klein recently co-authored an
essay
for
The Guardian,
sounding alarm about the dark worldview of politically insurgent tech
billionaires
like
Elon Musk
and
Peter Thiel
. Klein views these men — who are guiding
Donald Trump
’s presidency — as abandoning any positive vision for our collective future, and instead retrenching in preparation for a dark, nearly end times-level social collapse, from which they and other elites emerge unscathed, and all powerful. “The governing ideology of the far-right in our age of escalating disasters,” she writes, “has become a monstrous, supremacist survivalism.”
Rolling Stone
reached out to Klein for a conversation about Trump’s unique shock doctrine — as well as his administration’s confounding war on
science
and basic research. Klein is a professor at the University of British Columbia where she directs the Centre for Climate Justice. (You can almost forget she’s not American until you hear the pop of a hard ‘a’ when she says “against.”) Klein also offered her views on the recent Canadian election, and the legacy of Pope Francis, who invited her in 2015 to participate in the launch of his encyclical calling for a shared reverence of the glories of our Earth.
The following transcript has been edited for length and clarity.

For readers who are unfamiliar, can you quickly unpack the thesis of
The Shock Doctrine
?
In its simplest terms, the shock doctrine is just a strategy to advance deeply unpopular — and profitable — ideas. It’s using a moment of crisis to advance policies that benefit elites, but that tend to be opposed by most voters.
Trump’s trade war is certainly creating a shock. On some level, this protectionism runs counter to the GOP’s free-market free-for-all we’ve watched since Ronald Reagan. Yet on a macroeconomic level, it also looks like they’re trying to cool off the economy so they can justify jamming through their tax bill, which is the same old Republican wish list: tax breaks for the wealthy and cuts to the social safety net.
Look, there’s only so much I can do to make any of this seem rational. Because I do think we’re in an extreme phase — which is what I was trying to get at with that “
end times fascism
” piece.
What I’ve been tracking in the with
The Shock Doctrine
is a normie version of this. When people have public assets and social services, they tend to protect them. People tend to be opposed to water privatization; public transit privatization; Social Security privatization. So the right needs a crisis to exploit. You need an austerity crisis, or you need to do it in the name of bringing down inflation.
This is not a new phenomenon. I quote [the preeminent right-wing economist] Milton Friedman in the
Shock Doctrine,
saying, “Only a crisis, real or perceived, produces real change,” and when that crisis occurs, change “depends on the ideas that are lying around.”

He came up with that theory about how to advance his ideas, because he had seen the left do it during the Great Depression — when you had the social safety net emerge in the United States. People were trying to get at the root causes behind the Great Depression. Deregulated capitalism? Let’s regulate it. And let’s make sure nobody falls through the cracks six times. These were real attempts to solve crises.
But Friedman believed everything went wrong with the New Deal. So this was always a counter-revolution. The Friedman version of this was: Let’s be the ones who are ready. When the crisis occurs, let’s ram [our agenda] through. And then when it doesn’t do what it’s supposed to do, we’ll ram it through even harder.

总体来看，评论者们对政治领袖的行为、资本主义体系以及社会 dysfunction 的根源存在明显分歧，尤其是对精英政治的看法和经济体系的批评成为讨论的核心。

data.title: Analyzing Modern Nvidia GPU Cores
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 这篇文章分析了现代NVIDIA GPU核心，通过逆向工程揭示了其设计细节，包括指令调度策略、寄存器文件结构及其缓存、内存流水线特性等。研究表明，编译器引导硬件执行的硬件-编译器协同技术对GPU性能至关重要。文章还提出了一种基于流缓冲的简单指令预取器，并分析了寄存器文件缓存和读端口数量对仿真精度和性能的影响。新模型在执行周期上的平均绝对百分比误差（MAPE）比现有模拟器低18.24%，并在NVIDIA RTX A6000上验证了其有效性。此外，软件依赖管理机制在性能和面积上优于基于记分板的硬件机制。研究结果适用于其他NVIDIA架构，如Turing。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPU的功能和潜力

不同观点：
• **[winwang]** 认为GPU不仅擅长线性代数和浮点算术，并指出"uniform"寄存器和64位内存性能是显著的优点。他认为这些信息有助于消除对GPU功能的误解。

• **[kookamamie]** 则关注GPU型号的更新，指出NVIDIA RTX A6000已经落后两代，提到了更新的型号如6000 Ada和Pro 6000，暗示技术更新速度很快。

• **[nabla9]** 强调GPU架构依赖编译器来处理硬件依赖和性能优化，包括控制寄存器文件缓存分配策略，认为编译器在GPU性能中扮演关键角色。

• **[gmays]** 同意[nabla9]的观点，并称之为“特殊秘诀”，即编译器引导硬件执行的技术，认可编译器对GPU性能的重要性。

• **[gitroom]** 表示曾经认为GPU主要是计算工具，但现在意识到其功能远不止于此，并提出疑问是否有人能够完全发挥GPU的潜力，还是大多数人只是触及皮毛。

补充讨论：
• 对GPU功能的理解存在误解，部分人如[winwang]和[gitroom]认为公众对GPU的认识有限，尤其是其在处理非线性代数任务方面的能力。

• 对最新GPU技术的更新速度存在关注，如[kookamamie]指出型号更新频繁，提示技术发展迅速。

• 对GPU和编译器协同设计的讨论，如[nabla9]和[gmays]强调编译器在GPU架构中的重要作用，尤其是在处理数据依赖和性能优化方面。

争议焦点：
• 对GPU潜力的全面利用存在疑问，[gitroom]质疑是否有人能够完全发挥GPU的全部性能，反映出对实际应用中技术极限的关注。

• 对最新GPU型号的认知不同，[kookamamie]指出技术更新速度快，可能导致对硬件过时的担忧。

Title:
Analyzing Modern NVIDIA GPU cores
Authors:
Rodrigo Huerta
,
Mojtaba Abaie Shoushtary
,
José-Lorenzo Cruz
,
Antonio González
View a PDF of the paper titled Analyzing Modern NVIDIA GPU cores, by Rodrigo Huerta and 3 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
GPUs are the most popular platform for accelerating HPC workloads, such as artificial intelligence and science simulations. However, most microarchitectural research in academia relies on GPU core pipeline designs based on architectures that are more than 15 years old.
This paper reverse engineers modern NVIDIA GPU cores, unveiling many key aspects of its design and explaining how GPUs leverage hardware-compiler techniques where the compiler guides hardware during execution. In particular, it reveals how the issue logic works including the policy of the issue scheduler, the structure of the register file and its associated cache, and multiple features of the memory pipeline. Moreover, it analyses how a simple instruction prefetcher based on a stream buffer fits well with modern NVIDIA GPUs and is likely to be used. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of the register file cache and the number of register file read ports on both simulation accuracy and performance.
By modeling all these new discovered microarchitectural details, we achieve 18.24% lower mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) in execution cycles than previous state-of-the-art simulators, resulting in an average of 13.98% MAPE with respect to real hardware (NVIDIA RTX A6000). Also, we demonstrate that this new model stands for other NVIDIA architectures, such as Turing. Finally, we show that the software-based dependence management mechanism included in modern NVIDIA GPUs outperforms a hardware mechanism based on scoreboards in terms of performance and area.

data.title: Databricks in talks to acquire startup Neon for about $1B
data.author: ko_pivot
data.article_summary: 据2025年5月5日的报道，数据和人工智能独角兽公司Databricks正洽谈收购开源数据库引擎创业公司Neon，交易金额预计约10亿美元。尽管业内一些人认为交易接近完成，但谈判仍在进行中，仍可能失败。最终金额可能会因员工留任奖励而超过10亿美元。Neon公司及其CEO尚未回应置评请求，Databricks也拒绝评论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Databricks收购Neon及其影响

不同观点：
• 对Databricks收购行为的质疑：
  ◦ 有人认为Databricks收购bit.io后迅速关闭，表明其收购策略不明智，可能对Neon也会如此操作。
  ◦ 有人指出Databricks的商业决策不够透明，尤其是在成本和市场定位上。
  ◦ 对于Databricks是否能成功转型为AI公司存在怀疑，认为其在竞争中处于尴尬位置。

• 对Neon产品和其未来发展的看法：
  ◦ 有人高度评价Neon的产品，认为其在Postgres和serverless数据库领域具有独特优势，但担心被Databricks收购后会失去原有特色。
  ◦ 有人对Neon的商业模式表示担忧，不确定其是否能持续吸引用户付费。

• 对serverless和边缘数据库的批评：
  ◦ 有用户认为serverless和边缘数据库性能不如传统托管数据库，存在延迟和不稳定问题。
  ◦ 有人直接称这些技术为“骗局”，认为它们并不具备宣传中的优势。

• 对Databricks整体发展和未来方向的讨论：
  ◦ 有人对Databricks的未来表示怀疑，特别是其是否会上市以及是否能保持当前的增长速度。
  ◦ 有人提到Databricks试图通过收购来扩展其OLTP产品线，但对其具体战略表示困惑。

补充讨论：
• 有人提到科技公司近期的收购潮，暗示许多公司在2021年的高估值下融资，但现在面临上市困难，可能正在寻找退出策略。
• 有人对Neon团队的收购表示祝贺，但对其未来产品方向表示担忧，认为可能会失去原有用户的喜爱。

争议焦点：
• Databricks收购Neon是否能为其带来实际价值，还是会重蹈bit.io的覆辙。
• serverless和边缘数据库的真实性能和商业价值，用户体验与宣传效果的差距。

data.title: Modern LaTeX
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 《Modern LaTeX》是一本简短的LaTeX指南，旨在避免过时的内容，帮助用户快速上手这一广受欢迎的排版工具。书中介绍了如何使用LuaLaTeX进行安装和构建，建议使用如Garamond Premier等现代字体，并提供了构建命令和故障排除建议。指南的最新版本可在链接下载，并欢迎用户通过GitHub提交反馈。该书专注于实用性，避免了90年代以来不再相关的复杂细节，适合希望高效使用LaTeX的初学者和进阶用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对LaTeX及其替代品（如Typst、LyX、Org mode、Quarto等）的看法和使用体验

不同观点：
• BlackFly认为LaTeX应与HTML、CSS、JavaScript等网页技术对比，而不是与Word对比。他质疑LaTeX是否真正现代化，尤其是在响应式布局方面是否有所改进，并指出大多数人现在主要在线阅读文章。

• dev_l1x_be和多名其他用户（如__mharrison__、iNic）推荐使用Typst，认为它比LaTeX更现代化，编译速度更快，语法更简洁，且支持多种输出格式（如PDF、PNG、SVG、HTML）。不过，他们也提到Typst的用户群体相对较少。

• dochtman简短地表示Typst是“现代的LaTeX”，暗示Typst在功能上可以替代LaTeX，并且更符合当前用户的需求。

• cess11推荐使用LyX，认为它作为图形化编辑器能够满足大多数需求，并且可以向下兼容LaTeX，适合不想处理LaTeX复杂语法的新手用户。

• herewulf表示正在尝试使用Org mode结合LaTeX生成PDF，尤其是为了实现内容与格式分离，以便在多语言场景下生成一致的文档格式。

• qiu3344认为LaTeX虽然有些过时，但仍然非常强大，尤其是能够通过简单的文档类更改（如使用beamer制作演示文稿）。不过，他也提到现在更常用pandoc的Markdown进行写作，因为其可读性更强。

• agubelu对LaTeX持复杂态度，认为它既强大又令人头疼，表示虽然很高兴学过LaTeX，但以后不会再使用。

• aquafox表示虽然自己热爱LaTeX，但目前更倾向于使用Quarto，因为其更易用，支持“注入”LaTeX代码，并且更适合非技术合作者使用。

• watusername推荐Tectonic，认为它是LaTeX工具链中的一股新风，简化了LaTeX环境配置，但指出其选择XeTeX而非LuaTeX可能是个缺点。

• arthur-st分享了使用VSCode和LaTeX扩展的体验，并推荐使用TeX Live和LuaTeX引擎，认为这是目前和未来LaTeX用户的主流配置。

• agoose77推荐MyST引擎，认为它通过Markdown（特别是MyST扩展）处理文档结构化数据非常有用，并且给出了SciPy会议论文的具体例子。

• rochak分享了自己学习LaTeX时的负面体验，表示LaTeX让他在保持文档一致性方面非常困扰，甚至因此放弃了科研工作。

补充讨论：
- LaTeX的现代化问题：BlackFly和部分其他用户提到LaTeX在响应式设计和现代化布局方面缺乏进展，认为其应更适应现代在线阅读需求。
- 替代工具的兴起：Typst、LyX、Quarto等工具被多个用户推荐，显示出LaTeX用户正在寻找更简单、更现代的替代方案。
- 用户体验和学习曲线：一些用户（如rochak）提到LaTeX的学习曲线陡峭，而LyX、Org mode和Quarto等工具被认为对新手更加友好。
- 具体使用场景：不同用户根据自身需求（如多语言支持、科研论文、简历制作）选择不同的工具，显示出工具选择与具体应用场景密切相关。

Modern LaTeX
LaTeX is a tool for creating beautiful writing, or a torture device that drives
users to the brink of madness every time they see bad spacing for the rest
of their lives. One of the two. Despite origins that can be traced back four
decades, it remains one of the best typesetting programs around. Many of its
guides, however, haven't aged as well. This short book will get you started with
LaTeX without bogging you down in arcana that lost its relevance back in the 90s.
Where do I get it?
An up-to-date version should be available at
https://assets.bitbashing.io/modern-latex.pdf
How do I build it?
Install LuaLaTeX, a modern, Unicode-aware version of LaTeX.
On Linux, this is usually as simple as installing your distro's TeX Live
package, e.g.,
texlive-base
or
texlive-core
.
The same package should also provide the
latexmk
script.
(See below)
Check out the
online
branch of the source repository,
which is optimized for digital display instead of a printed book.
Changes include even margins, centered page numbers, a lack of blank pages
between chapters, and so on.
Change the fonts as-needed.
The official version of this book is typeset with Garamond Premier,
Neue Haas Grotesk, URW Futura, Drive Mono, Noto, and (of course) Latin Modern.
In the likely case that you don't have all of these typefaces,
change the
fontspec
commands (e.g.,
setmainfont
, etc.) appropriately,
then modify or remove the colophon at the back of the book.
Build the book using
latexmk -lualatex -latexoption=-halt-on-error modern-latex.tex
Note that
latexmk
will run LuaLaTeX multiple times, since
TeX generates cross references in one pass, then links them in a second.
If you can't use
latexmk
for some reason, you can manually invoke
lualatex -halt-on-error -shell-escape modern-latex.tex
until it no longer warns,
"Label(s) may have changed. Rerun to get cross-references right."
Feedback
...is welcome!
Please issue pull requests on this book's Github page,
or contact the author via matt <at> bitbashing.io
Enjoy!

data.title: Ty: A fast Python type checker and language server
data.author: arathore
data.article_summary: "ty" 是一个用 Rust 编写的高性能 Python 类型检查器和语言服务器。该项目仍在开发中，尚未达到生产可用阶段。贡献者可以通过在项目仓库中提交 issue 来反馈问题或参与开发，而拉取请求则应提交到 Ruff 仓库。项目采用 MIT 许可证，贡献代码即视为同意该许可条款。当前，项目包含 325 个星标和 3 个分支，主要使用 Python、Dockerfile 和 Shell 编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Astral推出的预发布Python类型检查工具"ty"及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• 支持与期待：
  - [zanie] 提到"ty"仍是预alpha版本，目前在验证发布流程，但对其未来表示期待，并预告将有更多更新。
  - [ngoldbaum] 对"ty"项目获得项目名称表示支持，并对Astral向PSF捐款表示赞赏。
  - [simlevesque] 已经从VSCode中移除了Mypy并开始使用"ty"，表示体验良好。

• 性能与比较：
  - [tmvphil] 比较了"ty"与mypy的速度，指出"ty"在检查大型项目时速度更快（0.5秒对比mypy的18秒），并发现了3500个错误。
  - [throwaway63467] 认为用Rust编写类型检查器是明显的方向，因为mypy速度较慢。

• 功能性与扩展性讨论：
  - [aleksanb] 指出mypy是目前唯一支持Django类型检查的工具，希望有更多工具像TypeScript一样接受现实中的代码复杂性，而不是只检查“应该使用”的结构。
  - [kodablah] 希望"ty"具有扩展性，指出Pyright和Mypy在扩展性方面的不足。
  - [cristea] 关心"ty"是否支持Django stubs，这是其公司切换工具的障碍。

• 市场与商业模式讨论：
  - [krupan] 好奇Astral是否找到了盈利模式。
  
• 工具集成与社区贡献：
  - [joshdavham] 询问是否计划创建官方的GitHub action，类似于ruff的集成。
  - [sestep] 询问"ty"是否与Red Knot是同一项目。
  - [rexledesma] 对"ty"作为新的Python语言服务器表示兴奋，尤其是在非官方VSCode分支中的应用潜力。

补充讨论：
• [f311a] 关心"ty"是否支持"go to definition"等语言服务器协议（LSP）功能，这是IDE集成的关键功能。
• [nickagliano] 提到Astral推出"ty"与Facebook发布Pyrefly的时间接近，注意到Rust在Python和JS工具领域的扩展趋势。

争议焦点：
• 工具的现实代码支持与理想设计之间的矛盾，尤其是对Django等复杂框架的支持。

data.title: Social AI companions pose unacceptable risks to teens and children under 18
data.author: CharlesW
data.article_summary: Common Sense Media发布了一篇文章，概述了其在媒体选择、数字公平、数字素养与公民意识、科技问责、健康童年等领域的工作与影响。文章还介绍了其人工智能（AI）计划和研究，包括与伦敦政治经济学院合作的数字公民课程评估，以及即将发布的2025年媒体使用普查。此外，Common Sense Media宣布了首个AI评级系统的框架，旨在帮助家长和教育者理解和应对青少年及儿童在家庭和学校中对生成式AI的采用。文章还简要介绍了其团队、合作伙伴及参与方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生成型AI和大型语言模型（LLMs）对成年人和儿童的情感影响及潜在风险

不同观点：
• lemoncookiechip认为，生成型AI对孤独的成年人可能构成较大风险，特别是在大城市中，成年人更难交朋友和改变自己。他们强调孤独的成年人是现实存在的问题，可能会沉迷于AI社交，就像沉迷于其他在线活动一样。不过，他们并不主张禁止或严格监管AI。

• blobbers质疑哪些具体产品在讨论范围内，认为像ChatGPT这样的工具并不擅长建立情感联系，但承认其他应用程序可能有这种能力。

• ohso4指出，即便父母想禁止孩子使用AI社交 companion，实际操作也很困难，因为孩子可以自行要求ChatGPT成为他们的社交伙伴。

• Der_Einzige持反对意见，认为有些人对AI社交companion的担忧是过度反应，并提到关于AI社交可能导致负面事件（如自杀）的媒体报道，暗示这些报道引发了不必要的恐慌。

• vincnetas抱怨由于未订阅而无法阅读相关文章，质疑这是否符合Hacker News的指导方针。

• bpodgursky认为，生成型AI对所有人（包括成年人和儿童）都构成不可接受的风险，但在西方社会，保护儿童的规范更加严格。

• baggy_trough讽刺那些想禁止向未成年人出售暴力视频游戏的人，暗示他们可能也是主张限制AI使用的人群。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的争议焦点包括AI作为社交伙伴对孤独成年人和儿童的潜在心理影响，以及是否应该对其进行监管或禁止。
• 另一个讨论点是媒体对AI相关负面事件的报道是否过度放大了风险。
• 还提到了实际操作中父母对孩子使用AI社交工具的管控困难。

• lemoncookiechip认为，生成型AI对孤独的成年人可能构成较大风险，特别是在大城市中，成年人更难交朋友和改变自己。他们强调孤独的成年人是现实存在的问题，可能会沉迷于AI社交，就像沉迷于其他在线活动一样。不过，他们并不主张禁止或严格监管AI。

• blobbers质疑哪些具体产品在讨论范围内，认为像ChatGPT这样的工具并不擅长建立情感联系，但承认其他应用程序可能有这种能力。

• ohso4指出，即便父母想禁止孩子使用AI社交 companion，实际操作也很困难，因为孩子可以自行要求ChatGPT成为他们的社交伙伴。

• Der_Einzige持反对意见，认为有些人对AI社交companion的担忧是过度反应，并提到关于AI社交可能导致负面事件（如自杀）的媒体报道，暗示这些报道引发了不必要的恐慌。

• vincnetas抱怨由于未订阅而无法阅读相关文章，质疑这是否符合Hacker News的指导方针。

• bpodgursky认为，生成型AI对所有人（包括成年人和儿童）都构成不可接受的风险，但在西方社会，保护儿童的规范更加严格。

• baggy_trough讽刺那些想禁止向未成年人出售暴力视频游戏的人，暗示他们可能也是主张限制AI使用的人群。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的争议焦点包括AI作为社交伙伴对孤独成年人和儿童的潜在心理影响，以及是否应该对其进行监管或禁止。
• 另一个讨论点是媒体对AI相关负面事件的报道是否过度放大了风险。
• 还提到了实际操作中父母对孩子使用AI社交工具的管控困难。

Today, after more than 13 years at the company, I am joining Cloudflareâs board of directors and retiring from my full-time position as CTO.
Back in 2012 I wrote a short post on my personal site simply titled:
Programmer
. The post announced that Iâd recently joined a company called CloudFlare (still sporting that capital âFâ) with the job title Programmer. Iâd chosen that title in part because it was the very first title Iâd ever had, and because it would reflect what Iâd be doing at Cloudflare.
I had spent a lot of time working at startupsâin technical and then management rolesâand wanted to go back to the really technical part that I loved most. Cloudflare gave me that opportunity, and I worked on a lot of systems that make up the Cloudflare that so many people around the world use today.
Looking back on my time at the company itâs really, really hard to pick my top highlights. In 2019
I wrote 6,000 words on the experience of helping build Cloudflare
. But here are five that stand out:
Always be shipping
The night we finished the preparation to launch
Universal SSL
sticks in my memory. We set out to offer the Industry's First Universal SSL for free, effectively doubling the size of the encrypted web overnight, a big deal in 2014. I remember Cloudflareâs third co-founder, Lee Holloway, hunched over his laptop finishing the code. The team has been working on it all weekend, and late that Sunday night Lee announced âitâs done.âÂ
Handling adversity
Itâs easy to pick moments of great success or when things went really well and
Cloudbleed in 2017
may not seem like a special moment, but it helped show who we were. It showed how a team could come together under intense stress, and how we could set the standard going forward for how companies disclose and talk about security problems. I personally discovered that a Google Meet call can be kept running for 24 hours and sleeping in two hour chunks is possible.
Being international and intentional
Originally from the UK, I was the first team member located outside the United States. I got to help build the largest offices outside the US: first, Cloudflareâs London office and then Cloudflareâs
Lisbon office
. These two offices are a big part of who we are today, with Lisbon being our European HQ.
When COVID halted our in-office work, I was blown away by the response from the team. As we all individually faced different difficulties because of the pandemic we continued to work together to ensure that the Internet, on which everyone was relying while confined at home, worked reliably and securely.
Truly impactful technology
Picking a favourite product would be a bit like asking someone to choose their favourite child, but I have soft spots for Cloudflareâs WAF, DNS, and DDoS solutions because I personally worked on those systems. And I still feel I need to apologize to the WAF team who took over my code and had to face that one Perl script that shall not be named!
Beyond the products thereâs something much deeper: Cloudflareâs mission to help build a better Internet. Iâve been very proud of how we have supported and advanced the Internet itself through our work on the latest standards and protocols. And Iâm even prouder of the role weâve played through Project Galileo, The Athenian Project, and Cloudflare for Campaigns.
The people
Every week Cloudflare holds an all-hands company meeting which ends with âShoutouts,â a chance to recognize members of the team who have gone above and beyond. Curiosity and empathy are two core values at Cloudflare, and I am struck every week by how often weâre recognizing teams of people who are being thanked for helping with a sale, fixing a bug, responding to an incident, or helping build Cloudflare. That team spirit is part of what makes Cloudflare a special place to work.
One of the things I will miss about not being at Cloudflare day-to-day is the incredible strength of the individual team members. Iâve been learning from them for 13 years straight!
Whatâs next
When I joined the company the team was a lot smaller! We were 25 people and now, weâve grown to more than 4,200 employees and 15 locations across the globe. As we grew I wore a lot of different hats. For a time I ran engineering, operations, security, and even IT. And, of course, I wrote for, and edited, the Cloudflare Blog for many, many years. Over time, we hired many great leaders to run those teams.
But the role that persisted was CTO. And today, we are announcing that, just as I gave up the title Programmer (and the programming that went along with it), I am giving up the title CTO (and the roleâs responsibilities) for a new way to help Cloudflare grow an

data.author: seam_carver
data.article_summary: Kindle Comic Converter (KCC) 是一款将漫画和漫画转换为电子书格式的工具，专为eink阅读器（如Kindle、Kobo、ReMarkable等）优化。它支持全屏无边界显示，并针对固定布局进行优化，特别适合eink屏幕的显示需求。KCC提供多种图像处理选项，并可根据设备屏幕分辨率缩放以优化文件大小和性能。支持的输入格式包括文件夹、CBZ、CBR、PDF等，输出格式包括MOBI、AZW3、EPUB、KEPUB和CBZ。该工具还提供了命令行版本和多种安装方式（如Windows、Mac、Docker等），并附有详细的使用说明和常见问题解答。KCC并非亚马逊官方工具，专为漫画/漫画读者设计，而非出版商。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对在电子墨水屏设备上阅读漫画的工具和脚本的评价及功能建议

不同观点：
• [支持与感谢] 多名用户（如sabslikesobs、w00ds、Mr_Eri_Atlov、janetmissed）对工具的开发和维护表示感谢，并认为该工具非常实用，解决了他们在电子书设备上阅读漫画的需求。
• [功能扩展建议] 用户shiandow建议将该工具与Calibre整合，认为这将增强其功能。tecleandor提出增加gamma/palette采样器功能，以便在不同配置下优化阅读体验。
• [使用体验与对比] ksynwa表示通常只使用Koreader进行自动裁剪和对比度调整，询问此工具是否有其他显著优势。looperhacks则提到过去在KOReader上遇到缩放问题，询问该工具是否能改善阅读体验。

补充讨论：
• [学习资源咨询] joshdavham借机询问如何学习PyQt，显示出对该框架的学习资源有需求。
• [设备兼容性问题] sepitus询问该工具是否适用于Remarkable设备，npteljes指出项目示例链接无法打开，looperhacks提到过去在Paperwhite 4上的不佳体验。
• [个人阅读计划] roskelld提到该工具可能帮助他完成阅读《Berserk》的计划，将工具与个人阅读习惯联系起来。

争议焦点：目前没有明显的争议，但有用户对工具的独特优势和设备兼容性存在疑问，显示出对功能改进和兼容性扩展的期待。

KCC
Kindle Comic Converter
optimizes comics and manga for eink readers like Kindle, Kobo, ReMarkable, and more.
Pages display in fullscreen without margins, with proper fixed layout support.
Its main feature is various optional image processing steps to look good on eink screens,
which have different requirements than normal LCD screens.
It also does filesize optimization by downscaling to your specific device's screen resolution,
which can improve performance on underpowered ereaders.
Supported input formats include folders/CBZ/CBR/PDF of JPG/PNG files and more.
Supported output formats include virtual panel view MOBI/AZW3, EPUB, KEPUB, and CBZ.
YouTube tutorial (please subscribe):
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IR2Fhcm9658
A word of warning
KCC
is not
Amazon's Kindle Comic Creator
nor is in any way endorsed by Amazon.
Amazon's tool is for comic publishers and involves a lot of manual effort, while
KCC
is for comic/manga readers.
KC2
in no way is a replacement for
KCC
so you can be quite confident we are going to carry on developing our little monster ;-)
Issues / new features / donations
If you have general questions about usage, feedback etc. please
post it here
.
If you have some
technical
problems using KCC please
file an issue here
.
If you can fix an open issue, fork & make a pull request.
If you find
KCC
valuable you can consider donating to the authors:
Ciro Mattia Gonano (founder, active 2012-2014):

Alex Xu (active 2023-Present)

, certificate by

DOWNLOADS
https://github.com/ciromattia/kcc/releases
Click on
Assets
of the latest release.
You probably want either
KCC_*.*.*.exe
(Windows)
kcc_macos_arm_*.*.*.dmg
(recent Mac with Apple Silicon M1 chip or later)
kcc_macos_i386_*.*.*.dmg
(older Mac with Intel chip)
The
c2e
and
c2p
versions are command line tools for power users.
On Windows 11, you may need to run in compatibility mode for an older Windows version.
On Mac, right click open to get past the security warning.
For flatpak, Docker, and AppImage versions, refer to the wiki:
https://github.com/ciromattia/kcc/wiki/Installation
FAQ
Windows 7 support

Image too dark?

Amazon USB File Transfer app

PREREQUISITES
You'll need to install various tools to access important but optional features. Close and re-open KCC to get KCC to detect them.
KindleGen

and
kindlegen

This is required for certain files and advanced features.
KCC will ask you to install if needed.

https://github.com/ciromattia/kcc/wiki/Installation#7-zip

data.title: Waiting for Postgres 18: Accelerating Disk Reads with Asynchronous I/O
data.author: lfittl
data.article_summary:
Postgres 18引入异步I/O（AIO），显著改变了I/O处理方式，尤其在云环境中能大幅提升性能。异步I/O允许并发处理多个读请求，无需等待每个请求完成，从而减少I/O等待时间。Postgres 17通过引入读流API为异步I/O打下基础，但仍依赖操作系统内核的预读取机制。Postgres 18则直接由数据库获取数据，绕过内核机制，提高I/O效率。

Postgres 18新增了`io_method`配置参数，控制I/O操作方式，包括：
1. `io_method = sync`：保持同步I/O模式。
2. `io_method = worker`：使用后台I/O工作进程处理读请求，不阻塞主进程。
3. `io_method = io_uring`：利用Linux的io_uring实现高效异步I/O。

在AWS上的测试显示，异步I/O使读取性能翻倍，io_uring表现尤为突出。当前版本AIO仅支持读操作，写操作仍为同步。用户需根据实际环境调整`io_method`和`effective_io_concurrency`以优化性能。

• [kev009] 指出FreeBSD的aio(4)已经做了大量工作，且没有Linux/glibc aio的缺点，对FreeBSD的异步I/O实现表示关注。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对Postgres、MariaDB和Percona数据库性能的比较需求。
• 在消费级硬件与企业级云服务上的异步I/O性能差异及其成本效益分析。
• 对更多并发连接功能的需求及pgbouncer的替代方案。

43916577.article_content:
Postgres shouldn’t feel like a black box:
Watch our product webinar
to see the latest features.
Waiting for Postgres 18: Accelerating Disk Reads with Asynchronous I/O
By
Lukas Fittl
May 07, 2025
With the Postgres 18 Beta 1 release this week a multi-year effort, and significant architectural shift in Postgres is taking shape:
Asynchronous I/O (AIO)
. These capabilities are still under active development, but they represent a fundamental change in how Postgres handles I/O, offering the potential for significant performance gains, particularly in cloud environments where latency is often the bottleneck.
Why asynchronous I/O matters
How Postgres 17’s read streams paved the way
New io_method setting in Postgres 18
io_method = sync
io_method = worker
io_method = io_uring
Asynchronous I/O in action
Benchmark on AWS: Doubling read performance & even greater gains from io_uring
Tuning effective_io_concurrency
Monitoring I/Os in flight with pg_aios
Heads Up: Async I/O makes I/O timing information hard to interpret
Conclusion
In summary
References
While some features may still be adjusted or dropped during the beta period before the final release, now is the best time to test and validate how Postgres 18 performs in practice. In Postgres 18 AIO is limited to read operations; writes remain synchronous, though support may expand in future versions.
In this post, we explain what asynchronous I/O is, how it works in Postgres 18, and what it means for performance optimization.
Why asynchronous I/O matters
Postgres has historically operated under a synchronous I/O model, meaning every read request is a blocking system call. The database must pause and wait for the operating system to return the data before continuing. This design introduces unnecessary waits on I/O, especially in cloud environments where storage is often network-attached (e.g. Amazon EBS) and I/O can have over 1ms of latency.
In a simplified model, we can illustrate the difference like this, ignoring any prefetching/batching the Linux kernel might do:
You can picture synchronous I/O like an imaginary librarian who retrieves one book at a time, returning before fetching the next. This inefficiency compounds as the number of physical reads for a logical operation increases.
Asynchronous I/O eliminates that bottleneck by allowing programs to issue multiple read requests concurrently, without waiting for prior reads to return. In an async program flow, I/O requests are scheduled to be read into a memory location and the program waits for completion of those reads, instead of issuing each read individually.
How Postgres 17’s read streams paved the way
The work for implementing asynchronous I/O in Postgres has been many years in the making. Postgres 17 introduced an essential internal abstration,
with the introduction of read stream APIs
. These internal changes standardized how read operations were issued across different subsystems and streamlined the use of
posix_fadvise()
to request that the operating system prefetch data in advance.
However, this advisory mechanism only hinted to the kernel to load data into the OS page cache, not into Postgres’ own shared buffers. Postgres still had to issue syscalls for each read, and OS readahead behaviour is not always consistent.
The upcoming Postgres 18 release removes this indirection. With true asynchronous reads, data is fetched directly into shared buffers by the database itself, bypassing reliance on kernel-level heuristics and enabling more predictable, higher-throughput I/O behavior.
New io_method setting in Postgres 18
To control the mechanism used for asynchronous I/O, Postgres 18 introduces a new configuration parameter:
io_method
. This setting determines how read operations are dispatched under the hood, and whether they’re handled synchronously, offloaded to I/O workers, or submitted directly to the kernel via
io_uring
.
The
io_method
setting must be set in postgresql.conf and cannot be changed without restarting. It controls which  I/O implementation Postgres will use and is essential to understand when tuning I/O performance in Postgres 18. There are three possible settings for io_method, with the current default (as of Beta 1) being
worker
.
io_method = sync
The
sync
setting in Postgres 18 mirrors the synchronous behavior as was implemented in Postgres 17. Reads are still synchronous and blocking, using
posix_fadvise()
to achieve read-ahead in the Linux kernel.
io_method = worker
The
worker
setting utilizes dedicated
I/O worker processes
running in the background that retrieve data independently of query execution. The main backend process enqueues read requests, and these workers interact with the Linux kernel to fetch data, which is then delivered into shared buffers,
without blocking the main process
.
The number of I/O workers can be configured through the new
io_workers
setting, and defaults to
3
. These workers are always running, and shared across all connections and databases.
io_method = io_uri

data.title: Create and edit images with Gemini 2.0 in preview
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: Google宣布在其AI开发平台Google AI Studio和Vertex AI中推出Gemini 2.0 Flash的图像生成预览功能。开发者现在可以使用Gemini API集成对话式图像生成与编辑，新版本在视觉质量、文字渲染和过滤器拦截率方面有显著改进。主要功能包括在不同环境中重新定位产品、实时协作编辑图像、对话式编辑图像特定部分、动态创建新产品SKU等。开发者可以通过Gemini Co-Drawing Sample App体验这些功能，并使用指定模型名在API中开始构建。Google计划未来进一步提升质量和扩展功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Gemini 2.0的多模态图像生成能力及其在市场上的表现和应用

不同观点：
• **vunderba**：将Gemini 2.0与OpenAI 4o、Midjourney 7等顶尖模型对比，认为其整体美学质量较Imagen 3.0显著下降，但多模态和速度是其优势。
• **eminence32**：指出使用文字描述生成图像时，常遇到表达限制，难以准确生成心中想象的图像，对会话式界面持怀疑态度。
• **minimaxir**：强调Gemini 2.0与Imagen 3在定价和功能上的差异，Gemini允许对话生成图像，而Imagen 3则更依赖于高质量的提示工程。
• **mNovak**：在共同绘画演示中遇到问题，模型对简笔画的识别不准确，生成结果不如预期。
• **pentagrama**：从社会角度反思，认为AI生成内容的大量涌现可能会冲击人类工艺和真实物品的价值。

补充讨论：
• **cush**：对共同绘画演示的趣味性给予积极评价。
• **thornewolf**：认为模型结果中等偏好，希望有更多已知良好工作流的参考资料。
• **qq99**：对多个版本的快速更新感到困惑，质疑AI Studio是否已有类似功能。
• **taylorhughes**：尽管图像编辑不如gpt-image-1，但速度的显著提升使得结果仍具吸引力。
• **egamirorrim**：在照片编辑中遇到困难，无法生成与原图相似的结果。
• **adverbly**：对Google的创新表示赞赏，但对其股票市场表现感到不解。
• **ohadron**：强调Gemini的速度优势，可能 unlock 更多使用场景。
• **refulgentis**：对Google频繁的版本发布和模型切换感到困惑，但也看到价格和控制上的改进。
• **GaggiX**：指出Gemini在欧盟不可用，认为其虽不如ChatGPT，但速度进步明显。
• **jansan**：对某些示例印象深刻，但对特定示例（如冰熊杯子）感到失望，认为共同绘画看起来像是仓促拼凑的。

争议焦点：
• Gemini 2.0的美学质量和实用性存在争议，部分用户认为其生成结果不如预期，而速度和多模态功能则被广泛认可。
• 用户对AI生成内容的质量和真实物品价值的冲击存在不同看法，部分用户对AI生成内容的大量涌现持批判态度。

• **refulgentis**：对Google频繁的版本发布和模型切换感到困惑，但也看到价格和控制上的改进。
• **GaggiX**：指出Gemini在欧盟不可用，认为其虽不如ChatGPT，但速度进步明显。
• **jansan**：对某些示例印象深刻，但对特定示例（如冰熊杯子）感到失望，认为共同绘画看起来像是仓促拼凑的。

• Gemini 2.0的美学质量和实用性存在争议，部分用户认为其生成结果不如预期，而速度和多模态功能则被广泛认可。
• 用户对AI生成内容的质量和真实物品价值的冲击存在不同看法，部分用户对AI生成内容的大量涌现持批判态度。

data.title: Telling Lies: Bowie and Online Music Distribution in 1996
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary: 1996年，尽管在线音乐零售通过网站如Music Boulevard和CDnow蓬勃发展，但音乐下载和流媒体仍面临挑战。大卫·鲍伊（David Bowie）在当年9月通过其网站提供单曲《Telling Lies》的免费下载，成为在线音乐分发的早期试验。N2K公司试图通过互联网直接分发音乐，绕过唱片公司。然而，由于当时带宽有限，音乐文件下载困难且质量较低。尽管提供了多种格式，包括通过Liquid Audio提供的CD质量文件，下载时间长且需要专用软件播放。此次尝试展示了互联网对音乐分发模式的潜在影响，但技术限制使其难以实现理想效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：音乐行业的数字化转型与早期在线音乐发行的先锋和技术发展

不同观点：
• burningChrome 认为 Prince 是音乐行业变革的先锋，他预见了单曲销售的未来，并影响了 iTunes 单曲销售模式的发展。他提到 Prince 希望根据自己的节奏发布音乐，而不是遵循传统的专辑发布模式。
• dhosek 指出 1999 年 Napster 的出现标志着在线音乐分发的兴起，并提到在 iPod 出现之前，数字音乐的播放选择非常有限。
• buildsjets 认为 Aerosmith 在 1994 年通过 Compuserve 发布在线音乐，才是真正的在线音乐发行先锋，比 David Bowie 早了几年。
• zirkonit 支持 David Bowie 是互联网音乐先锋的观点，提到 Bowie 在 1994 年就有了自己的网站，并在 1998 年推出了自己的 ISP。
• bdcravens 描述了 1997-1998 年间在 486 电脑上播放 MP3 文件的困难，需要退出 Windows 进入 DOS 系统。

补充讨论：
• neilv 提到 Bowie 参与的在线聊天活动，用户需要辨别哪个是真正的 Bowie，这与今天的社交媒体管理有相似之处。
• LaundroMat 解释了专辑存在的部分原因是由于分销成本的考虑，生产和储存单曲光盘的成本较高。
• Animats 提到文章未详细描述电子商务的实现，并引导读者购买相关书籍以了解更多。
• fallinditch 提到 Bowie 尝试了鼓打贝斯风格，并指出他是第一个将音乐目录出售给投资工具的艺术家。
• bitwize 讨论了盗版对音乐分发的影响，指出盗版网络在 Napster 之前就已经存在，并影响了早期的音乐分发模式。
• dirtyhippiefree 批评了 RIAA 起诉粉丝的策略，认为这并不是一个好主意。
• helpfulContrib 分享了 1996 年创建跨国在线音乐服务的经历，并提到该社区对地下音乐的发展贡献。

争议焦点：
• 关于谁是音乐行业数字化转型的真正先锋存在争议，主要集中在 Prince、Aerosmith 和 David Bowie 之间。不同用户提供了各自的例子和论据支持其观点。

43917376.article_content:
Telling Lies: Bowie and Online Music Distribution in 1996
Online music retail was thriving by 1996, thanks to sites like Music Boulevard and CDnow. But music downloads and streaming was more of a challenge — as David Bowie discovered in September 1996.
By
Richard MacManus
|
May 7, 2025
| Tags:
Dot-com
,
1996
The CD version of David Bowie's online single, 'Telling Lies', 1996;
via kupindo.com
.
In an interview featured in the 1998 book “The Interactive Music Handbook,” Larry Rosen — CEO of an online music services company called N2K — provided his theory on how the internet would overhaul the music distribution system.
“The model that’s eventually going to prevail is one where the artist is going to finance her own record, produce it, and divide the distribution rights up.”
After explaining that the artist will no longer need to be signed to a record company for multiple years, Rosen said she would instead “go to a company like N2K and have us distribute the record electronically, or to all the people you have online in those particular areas, and we’re going to receive “X” percentage of these sales.”
So that was the goal of
David Bowie’s digital partner, N2K
: to distribute an artist’s music online and cut out the middlemen, a.k.a. the record labels. After all, the primary task of a record label was to distribute music, so surely they would no longer be needed when the internet matured?
David Bowie's website, October 1996;
via Wayback Machine
.
By 1996, the
retail part of online music existed
, but not the electronic distribution part. At that time, buying music online meant purchasing a CD — or some other physical format provided by a record label — on a retail website like Music Boulevard (owned by N2K) or CDnow (its arch-rival).
Although the pioneering
Internet Underground Music Archive
had proven that downloading music as a digital file was possible, the low bandwidth of the era made it hugely impractical. But Rosen thought that, eventually, records would be able to be “electronically transmitted” over the internet — “you would take those sounds and convert them into bits and send them to somebody on the other end, on a global basis, and they would store it.”
CDnow website, October 1996;
via Wayback Machine
.
(Incidentally, IUMA co-founder
Rob Lord became
“the new Vice President of Rock Sites for N2K Entertainment” at around the same time N2K acquired Rocktropolis.)
Telling Lies
The first test of this theory with a major music artist was, naturally, David Bowie. In September 1996, Bowie’s latest single “Telling Lies” was made available as a free download on the N2K-produced website, davidbowie.com.
Bowie's 'Telling Lies' single on his website, circa September 1996;
via Wayback Machine
.
The song was uploaded to the site on 11 September, 1996, and two remixes followed later. MP3 wasn’t an established online music file format at the time, but fans could access the song in eight other formats, according to
a later New York Times report
. The easiest option was to stream the song on the site, using RealAudio or Shockwave audio. These were low quality files, to try and minimise buffering.
There were also mpeg versions available, probably MP2, although these too were relatively low quality. One user on the Bowie newsgroup reported three mpeg versions (5Mb, 3.8Mb and 1.3Mb). Another said she tried to download the 5MB version using AOL “and the download quit after about 2 hours and gave me only about 4.2 MB.” She was able to listen to “about 4 1/2 minutes of the song from this incomplete file,” but
noted that
“the sound quality seems pretty bad.”
The different versions of Bowie's 'Telling Lies' single;
via Wayback Machine
.
If you wanted higher quality, you could download a 16-bit CD-quality file that “took 45 minutes to grab with a 28.8 Kbps modem” (according to the Times). This was provided by Liquid Audio, a new company founded earlier that year by Gerry Kearby, a native of Redwood City, California. Kearby, who had
previously worked
as an audio technician for bands like The Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane, wanted to create an online distribution technology that included copyright protection features. To achieve this, the company
partnered with Dolby Labs
for the compression technology and
added its own
watermarking and digital signatures.
The Liquid Audio version of “Telling Lies” was a
9.7MB zip file
, which opened to reveal a 9.9MB .la1 file (which
stood for
“Liquid Audio File”). That zip file would have taken at least 45 minutes to download over a 28.8 Kbps modem — but probably more than that, given how variable bandwidth was over dial-up. The user would then have needed the Liquid Audio player software to play the song.
N2K's e_mod website, where people could download Liquid Audio File music.
Some users reported not being able to access the site at all. “Maybe the site is just too busy or something, but all I've been getting are server errors and the like,” wrote one disappointed fan
on alt.fan.davi

data.title: Mistral ships le chat – enterprise AI assistant that can run on prem
data.author: _lateralus_
data.article_summary: Mistral AI推出Le Chat Enterprise，这是一款功能丰富的AI助手，基于全新的Mistral Medium 3模型，旨在解决企业AI面临的工具分散、知识整合不安全、模型僵化以及投资回报慢等挑战。Le Chat Enterprise提供统一的AI平台，包括企业搜索、代理构建器、自定义数据和工具连接器、文档库、自定义模型和混合部署等功能。该平台注重隐私保护，支持自托管和云部署，具有高度可定制性和控制力，并提供全面的审计日志和存储功能。企业可以通过Le Chat连接到Google Drive、Sharepoint等多个系统，快速获取个性化答案，并利用AI自动化常规任务。Le Chat Enterprise现已在Google Cloud Marketplace上线，并将陆续登陆Azure AI和AWS Bedrock。用户可通过chat.mistral.ai体验或下载移动应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mistral模型及相关技术产品的发布及其影响

不同观点：
• **支持Mistral的观点**：
   - [codingbot3000] 认为Mistral在数据隐私方面具有优势，并指出可以在Mac上的Docker中运行Mistral。
   - [_pdp_] 支持Mistral，但同时强调多样化模型的重要性，认为不同模型在不同任务上有其独特优势。
   - [I_am_tiberius] 表示更信任Mistral（"le chat"），认为在信息安全方面比OpenAI更可靠。
   - [phupt26] 提到Mistral的新模型（Medium 3）表现优秀，并提供了相关链接。
   - [guerrilla] 认为Mistral的发布是欧洲在技术领域竞争中的重要一步，对此持积极态度。

• **质疑Mistral的观点**：
   - [iamnotagenius] 认为Mistral模型的表现不如其他开源模型，特别是在上下文处理、语言表达和编码方面存在不足，不如中国和美国的竞品模型。

• **其他技术产品的比较**：
   - [FuriouslyAdrift] 提到GPT4All已经能够本地运行，质疑Mistral的独特性。
   - [victorbjorklund] 直接质疑为何要使用Mistral而不是其他开源模型。

• **实际应用的观点**：
   - [curiousgal] 认为Mistral的发布“太少也太晚”，其所在的公司已经在使用Anthropic's Claude，暗示Mistral在企业市场上的竞争力可能不足。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论如[m-hodges]和[caseyy]并未直接讨论技术细节，而是提及了翻译趣闻和Mistral可能引发的文化现象（如meme），属于非技术性讨论。
• 评论中提到了多个相关链接，如Mistral Medium 3的讨论链接和相关新闻链接，表明讨论者引用了外部信息来支持自己的观点。

争议焦点：
• Mistral模型相较于其他开源模型的竞争力和独特性受到质疑，特别是在性能和实际应用中的表现。

data.title: Show HN: 100.st – Dev utilities I built for format conversions and encoding
data.author: abdelbkk
data.article_summary: 100.st 是一个多功能开发者工具集，旨在提升工作效率。它提供各种格式转换工具，如 JSON、YAML、XML、CSV 之间的互转，以及 UUID 生成工具（NIL, V1, V4, V7）。此外，还包括大小写转换（camelCase, kebab-case, snake_case 等）、文本编码工具（Text to Hex, ASCII to Text）、网络工具（生成 IPv4, IPv6, Mac 地址）和文本处理工具（删除空行、添加前后缀等）。该平台涵盖了开发者常用的多种实用功能，简化了日常操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对多个在线工具集的功能、设计和必要性的不同看法

不同观点：
• [bh213] 分享了一个专注于自动检测和仅在浏览器中运行的工具集链接，展示了自己的项目。
• [putna] 回应称自己也有一个个人工具集，并分享了链接，强调了快捷键操作（Cmd+K）。
